programs.name: SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program)
programs.summary: Monthly grocery benefits on an EBT card for people with low income.
programs.whoQualifies: Based on household income, size, expenses, and immigration/citizenship status. Most able-bodied adults without dependents must meet work requirements. Eligibility rules vary by state.
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income (pay stubs or benefit letters); proof of residency (utility bill or lease); Social Security numbers for household members; immigration documents if not a U.S. citizen.
programs.howToApply: Apply online through your state's SNAP office (find it via the official link below), by phone, or in person at a local office. You will usually complete an interview by phone or in person before benefits are approved.
programs.localHelp: Call 2-1-1 or contact your state SNAP office and local community action agency for application help.

programs.name: WIC (Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children)
programs.summary: Free healthy food, nutrition education, and breastfeeding support for pregnant people, new parents, and children under 5.
programs.whoQualifies: Pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding people, and infants and children up to age 5, who meet income guidelines and have a nutrition need. Many working families qualify.
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income; proof of residency; proof of pregnancy or child's age (birth certificate, medical record); immunization records for children.
programs.howToApply: Call your local WIC clinic to schedule an eligibility appointment. Appointments include a short health and nutrition screening.
programs.localHelp: Use the WIC clinic locator at the official site below, or call 2-1-1.

programs.name: National School Lunch and School Breakfast Programs
programs.summary: Free or low-price breakfast and lunch at school for eligible children.
programs.whoQualifies: Children in participating schools; based on household income or participation in SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR. Some schools offer free meals to all students (Community Eligibility Provision).
programs.documents: School meal application form (from your school district); proof of income if required; SNAP/TANF case number if categorical eligible.
programs.howToApply: Fill out a school meal application at your child's school or school district office. Apply any time during the school year.
programs.localHelp: Contact your child's school or school district nutrition office.

programs.name: SUN Bucks (Summer EBT)
programs.summary: Groceries benefit for families with school-age children during summer months.
programs.whoQualifies: Children eligible for free or reduced-price school meals, including through SNAP, TANF, or Medicaid participation, depending on the state.
programs.documents: Usually automatic if already enrolled in SNAP, TANF, or free school meals; otherwise a state application with child's information and proof of eligibility.
programs.howToApply: Most states issue benefits automatically to eligible families. Check with your state's Summer EBT/SUN Bucks office to confirm or apply.
programs.localHelp: Contact your state education agency or Summer EBT office; schools can also help.

programs.name: Medicaid
programs.summary: Free or low-cost health coverage for adults, children, pregnant people, seniors, and people with disabilities who meet income rules.
programs.whoQualifies: Based on income, household size, disability, pregnancy, or age. Rules vary by state; some states expanded Medicaid to cover more low-income adults.
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income; Social Security number; proof of citizenship or immigration status; proof of residency; pregnancy or disability documents if applicable.
programs.howToApply: Apply online through HealthCare.gov or your state Medicaid agency, by phone, by mail, or in person at a local Medicaid office.
programs.localHelp: Call 2-1-1, visit a local Department of Human/Social Services office, or get free help from a Navigator or certified application counselor.

programs.name: CHIP (Children's Health Insurance Program)
programs.summary: Low-cost health and dental coverage for children in families that earn too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private insurance.
programs.whoQualifies: Children up to age 19 in families within state income limits. Pregnant people may be covered in some states.
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income; children's Social Security numbers or immigration documents; proof of residency.
programs.howToApply: Apply through your state Medicaid/CHIP agency, HealthCare.gov, InsureKidsNow.gov, or by phone/in person at a local office.
programs.localHelp: Call 1-877-KIDS-NOW (1-877-543-7669) or visit InsureKidsNow.gov for state contact information.

programs.name: Medicare
programs.summary: Federal health insurance for people 65+, younger people with disabilities, and people with end-stage renal disease.
programs.whoQualifies: Age 65 or older with sufficient work history (or spouse's); younger with SSDI for 24 months; any age with ALS or end-stage renal disease.
programs.documents: Social Security number; proof of age/citizenship; current health insurance information; work history records.
programs.howToApply: Apply online at SSA.gov, by phone at 1-800-772-1213, or in person at a Social Security office. Initial enrollment windows apply; late enrollment may cost more.
programs.localHelp: Contact your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) for free, one-on-one Medicare counseling.

programs.name: HRSA-Funded Health Centers
programs.summary: Community clinics providing primary medical, dental, and mental health care on a sliding fee scale based on income.
programs.whoQualifies: Open to everyone, including people without insurance; uninsured and underinsured patients pay based on income and family size.
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income (for sliding-fee discount); insurance card if you have one.
programs.howToApply: Walk in or call to become a patient. Ask about the sliding-fee scale application at your first visit.
programs.localHelp: Find a nearby health center using the locator below.

programs.name: Housing Choice Voucher Program (Section 8)
programs.summary: Rental assistance that helps very low-income families, seniors, and people with disabilities afford private-market housing.
programs.whoQualifies: Based on gross annual income and family size (generally below 50% of area median income). U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens.
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income; Social Security numbers for all household members; proof of residency; birth certificates for children.
programs.howToApply: Apply through your local Public Housing Agency (PHA). Many waiting lists are long or closed; check which PHAs are accepting applications.
programs.localHelp: Contact your local Public Housing Agency or HUD office.

programs.name: LIHEAP (Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program)
programs.summary: Help paying home heating and cooling bills, plus weatherization and crisis assistance for shutoff prevention.
programs.whoQualifies: Based on household income (generally at or below 150% of federal poverty level or 60% of state median income). Rules vary by state.
programs.documents: Photo ID; recent utility bills; proof of income; proof of residency; Social Security numbers.
programs.howToApply: Apply through your state LIHEAP office or local community action agency before funds run out for the year.
programs.localHelp: Contact your local community action agency or call 2-1-1.

programs.name: Public Housing
programs.summary: Government-owned rental homes for low-income families, seniors, and people with disabilities, with rent based on income.
programs.whoQualifies: Low-income families, seniors, and people with disabilities who are U.S. citizens or eligible non-citizens. Background checks apply.
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income; Social Security numbers; birth certificates; landlord references if requested.
programs.howToApply: Apply through your local Public Housing Agency. Waiting lists are common and may be closed.
programs.localHelp: Contact your local Public Housing Agency.

programs.name: Lifeline
programs.summary: Monthly discount on phone or internet service for qualifying low-income households.
programs.whoQualifies: Based on income or participation in SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Veterans Pension, or certain Tribal programs. One benefit per household.
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income or proof of participation in a qualifying program; address information.
programs.howToApply: Apply online at LifelineSupport.org or through a participating phone/internet company.
programs.localHelp: Contact participating wireless or internet providers in your area; call 2-1-1 for help.

programs.name: TANF (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families)
programs.summary: Short-term cash assistance and support services for families with children.
programs.whoQualifies: Families with minor children (or pregnant people) meeting income and resource limits; work participation requirements usually apply.
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income and resources; children's birth certificates and Social Security numbers; proof of residency.
programs.howToApply: Apply at your state or local TANF/welfare office, often online or in person.
programs.localHelp: Contact your state TANF office or local Department of Human/Social Services.

programs.name: SSI (Supplemental Security Income)
programs.summary: Monthly cash payments for people aged 65+, blind, or disabled with limited income and resources.
programs.whoQualifies: Age 65+, blind, or disabled, with limited income and resources; U.S. citizens or certain eligible non-citizens.
programs.documents: Social Security card/number; birth certificate; proof of income and resources (bank statements); medical records for disability; proof of living arrangement.
programs.howToApply: Apply online at SSA.gov (for adults), by phone at 1-800-772-1213, or in person at a Social Security office.
programs.localHelp: Visit a local Social Security office; call 1-800-772-1213 to schedule.

programs.name: SSDI (Social Security Disability Insurance)
programs.summary: Monthly benefits for people with a qualifying disability who have worked and paid Social Security taxes long enough.
programs.whoQualifies: Workers with a qualifying disability and sufficient work credits; certain family members may also receive benefits.
programs.documents: Social Security number; birth certificate; W-2s or tax returns; medical records and doctors' reports; work history.
programs.howToApply: Apply online at SSA.gov, by phone at 1-800-772-1213, or in person at a Social Security office.
programs.localHelp: Contact a local Social Security office or a disability advocate/attorney for application help.

programs.name: Unemployment Insurance (UI)
programs.summary: Temporary weekly payments for workers who lost a job through no fault of their own.
programs.whoQualifies: Unemployed or partially unemployed workers who meet state wage and work-history requirements and are able and available to work.
programs.documents: Social Security number; driver's license or state ID; employment history for the past 18 months (employer names, addresses, dates); reason for separation.
programs.howToApply: File a claim with your state unemployment agency online, by phone, or in person soon after losing your job.
programs.localHelp: Contact your state unemployment office or local American Job Center.

programs.name: Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF)
programs.summary: Subsidized child care vouchers to help low-income parents work, attend training, or go to school.
programs.whoQualifies: Parents or caregivers with children under 13 (or up to 19 if disabled) who meet income limits and activity requirements (work, job search, or education).
programs.documents: Photo ID; proof of income; proof of work, school, or training; children's birth certificates and immunization records.
programs.howToApply: Apply through your state or tribal child care agency. Waiting lists are common.
programs.localHelp: Contact your state child care subsidy agency or local child care resource and referral agency.

programs.name: Head Start and Early Head Start
programs.summary: Free early childhood education, health, nutrition, and family support services for young children.
programs.whoQualifies: Children from birth to age 5 from low-income families; children in foster care, homeless children, and children receiving SSI are categorically eligible.
programs.documents: Child's birth certificate; proof of income; proof of residency; immunization records.
programs.howToApply: Apply directly with a local Head Start program; enrollment is often year-round.
programs.localHelp: Use the Head Start locator below to find a program near you.

programs.name: Federal Pell Grants (via FAFSA)
programs.summary: Need-based grant money for college or career school that does not have to be repaid.
programs.whoQualifies: U.S. citizens or eligible non-citizens with financial need enrolled in an eligible degree or certificate program; must maintain satisfactory academic progress.
programs.documents: Social Security number; federal tax returns; records of untaxed income; FSA ID to sign the FAFSA online.
programs.howToApply: Complete the FAFSA at StudentAid.gov each year you are in school. List the schools you want to attend.
programs.localHelp: Contact your school's financial aid office or call 1-800-4-FED-AID.

programs.name: Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) and Free Tax Prep (VITA)
programs.summary: A refundable tax credit for low- to moderate-income workers, plus free tax return preparation through VITA.
programs.whoQualifies: Workers with earned income below IRS limits, with or without qualifying children; must file a tax return to claim it.
programs.documents: Social Security numbers for everyone on the return; W-2s and other income documents; prior-year tax return if available; bank account for direct deposit.
programs.howToApply: File a federal tax return and claim the EITC. For free preparation, visit a VITA site (income limits usually $67,000 or less).
programs.localHelp: Find a VITA site via the IRS locator or call 2-1-1.

programs.name: VA Health Care
programs.summary: Medical, mental health, and specialty care for eligible veterans at VA clinics and hospitals.
programs.whoQualifies: Veterans who served on active duty and were discharged under conditions other than dishonorable; eligibility priority groups based on service history, disability, and income.
programs.documents: DD214 (discharge papers); photo ID; income and insurance information; military service records.
programs.howToApply: Apply online at VA.gov, by phone, by mail, or in person at a VA medical center.
programs.localHelp: Contact your nearest VA medical center or a Veterans Service Organization (VSO) for free claims and enrollment help.

programs.name: VA Disability Compensation
programs.summary: Monthly tax-free payments for veterans with disabilities connected to military service.
programs.whoQualifies: Veterans with a current illness or injury that happened or got worse during active service, and a discharge other than dishonorable.
programs.documents: DD214; service medical records; current medical records; doctor opinions linking condition to service (for some claims).
programs.howToApply: File a claim online at VA.gov, by mail, in person at a VA office, or with the help of an accredited representative.
programs.localHelp: Contact a Veterans Service Organization (VSO), VA regional office, or accredited claims agent for free help.

programs.name: VA Pension (including Aid and Attendance)
programs.summary: Needs-based monthly payments for wartime veterans with limited income who are 65+ or permanently disabled; higher amounts for those needing aid and attendance.
programs.whoQualifies: Wartime veterans meeting service, age/disability, and income/net-worth limits; discharged under conditions other than dishonorable.
programs.documents: DD214; proof of income and assets; medical evidence; proof of unreimbursed medical expenses.
programs.howToApply: Apply online at VA.gov or by mail using VA Form 21P-527EZ.
programs.localHelp: Contact a VA regional office or accredited Veterans Service Organization.

programs.name: GI Bill (VA Education Benefits)
programs.summary: Education and training benefits for veterans, service members, and qualifying family members.
programs.whoQualifies: Based on length and type of service; Post-9/11 GI Bill, Montgomery GI Bill, and dependents' programs have different rules.
programs.documents: DD214; school enrollment information; transcripts if transferring credits.
programs.howToApply: Apply online at VA.gov, by mail, or in person at a VA regional office.
programs.localHelp: Contact the school's certifying official or a VA education counselor.

programs.name: State Vocational Rehabilitation Services
programs.summary: Free job training, counseling, and employment services to help people with disabilities get and keep jobs.
programs.whoQualifies: People with a physical or mental disability that creates a substantial barrier to employment, who can benefit from VR services.
programs.documents: Photo ID; disability documentation or medical records; Social Security number; education and work history.
programs.howToApply: Contact your state vocational rehabilitation agency to schedule an intake appointment.
programs.localHelp: Find your state VR agency using the directory below.

programs.name: Social Security Ticket to Work
programs.summary: Free employment support for Social Security disability beneficiaries (SSDI or SSI) who want to work, including job training, career counseling, and job placement.
programs.whoQualifies: People ages 18 through 64 who receive SSDI or SSI benefits because of a disability.
programs.documents: Social Security number; proof of SSDI or SSI benefit (award letter); photo ID.
programs.howToApply: Call the Ticket to Work Help Line or choose an Employment Network (EN) or State Vocational Rehabilitation agency as your service provider through the Choose Work website.
programs.localHelp: Call the Ticket to Work Help Line at 1-866-968-7842 or visit choosework.ssa.gov to find a local Employment Network.
